title: 7.4.4 Lab: Fly and fire
description: The ship slides off the canvas and Space does nothing. Keep the ship on the canvas with two ifs, fire on a cooldown, and delete the shots that leave the top.

steps.title: Keep the ship on the canvas
steps.instructions: Hold left for a while: the ship slides off the canvas. In `moveShip()`, after the two lines that move it, add two ifs that put it back: when `ship.x` is less than 20, set it to 20; when it is more than 380, set it to 380. The ship is 36 pixels wide and `x` is its centre, so 20 keeps all of it on the screen.
hints: The second if is the same shape, with `>` and 380.

steps.title: Fire on a cooldown
steps.instructions: In `fire()`, first count `cooldown` down: take 1 off it while it is above 0. Then, when Space is held **and** `cooldown` is 0, build a shot: a 6 by 14 sprite at `(ship.x, ship.y - 18)` with `collider = 'none'` (so it passes through things, as in 5.2.23) and the colour `'yellow'`. Push it onto `bullets`, then set `cooldown` to 12 so the next shot has to wait 12 frames. Hold Space: the shots should come about five a second, evenly spaced.
hints: `if (cooldown > 0) cooldown -= 1;` is the countdown, from 7.4.2. Leave out the `if` and `cooldown` runs on below 0, so `cooldown === 0` is never true again and the ship cannot fire.
`if (kb.pressing('space') && cooldown === 0) { ... }` is the test, from 7.4.3. The sprite, the push and `cooldown = 12;` all go inside its braces.

steps.title: Shots that leave are deleted
steps.instructions: Every shot climbs 8 pixels a frame and never stops. In the loop in `moveBullets()`, a shot whose `y` is less than -20 has left the top: delete it and splice it out of `bullets`, as Flappy did with its pipes in 5.11.3. The loop runs from the end of the array to the start because a splice moves every later shot down one place; going backwards, none is skipped. Hold Space and watch 'shots alive' at the top: it should stay at 4 or fewer. If it keeps climbing, shots are not being removed.
hints: `bullets[i].delete();` takes the shot off the screen and `bullets.splice(i, 1);` takes it out of the array. You need both.

requirements.title: The ship stays on the canvas
requirements.description: Two ifs in moveShip() put the ship back when it passes either side: x no smaller than 20 and no bigger than 380. Help: 7.4.2 (Reading: A ship, and a timer you start yourself)

requirements.title: The cooldown counts down
requirements.description: fire() takes 1 off cooldown on every frame it is above 0, and never below 0: a countdown that runs past 0 never reaches 0 again, so the ship could not fire. Help: 7.4.2 (Reading: A ship, and a timer you start yourself)

requirements.title: A shot is made only when Space is held and the cooldown is 0
requirements.description: The shot is pushed onto bullets inside an if that asks both, joined with &&: Space is held, and cooldown is 0. Help: 7.4.3 (Worked Example: Fire with a cooldown)

requirements.title: Firing sets the cooldown again
requirements.description: Next to the push, cooldown is set back to 12 (any number above 0), so the next shot has to wait. Help: 7.4.3 (Worked Example: Fire with a cooldown)

requirements.title: Shots that leave the top are deleted and spliced out
requirements.description: Inside an if that asks whether a shot's y is above the top, the shot is deleted from the screen and spliced out of bullets. Help: 5.11.3 (Lab: Pipes that come and go)

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your code
aiCheck.prompt: The student wrote a moSHion sketch (p5-style JavaScript with a physics world) for the lab "7.4.4 Lab: Fly and fire". The task they were given: Three functions to finish. In moveShip(), after the two lines that move the ship, add two ifs so ship.x never goes below 20 or above 380. In fire(), first count cooldown down by 1 while it is above 0; then, when Space is held AND cooldown is 0, build a 6 by 14 yellow shot with collider 'none' just above the ship, push it onto bullets, and set cooldown to 12. In moveBullets(), inside the loop that already runs from the end of bullets to the start, a shot whose y is less than -20 has left the top: delete its sprite and splice it out of bullets. You cannot run their code: read it and judge what it WOULD do when the sketch runs. moSHion facts that matter here: setup() runs once; draw() runs about 60 times a second, and so does every function it calls. kb.presses('space') is true only on the one frame a key goes down; kb.pressing('space') is true on every frame it is held. y grows downward. In this game draw() calls the game's own functions every frame, inside if (playing) { ... }. sprite.delete() (its other name is remove()) takes a sprite off the screen, and array.splice(i, 1) takes it out of the array; a shot or enemy that is gone has to leave both the screen and the array. A loop that runs from the end of an array to the start never skips an item when one is spliced out. overlaps() asks whether two sprites touch right now and changes nothing; it works for sprites with collider 'none', and colliding() never sees such a sprite. drawTop() runs after the sprites are drawn, so its words sit on top; text drawn in draw() lands underneath the sprites. A shot that climbs has a y that gets smaller, and leaves the top once y is below 0. Judge each criterion by whether the idea is achieved, however the student wrote it. Different variable, parameter and helper-function names, template strings, arrow functions, a ternary or an if/else chain, x++ or x += 1 or x = x + 1, semicolons, spacing, quotes and order are all fine. Names that other code in the program already calls (moveShip, fire, moveBullets) must keep those names, because a renamed one is never called. Do not require any particular structure unless the criterion names one. Mark a criterion missing only when the idea is absent or the code does the opposite. Code inside a comment or a string never runs, and the STEP comments the starter came with are not the student's work. The starter's moveShip(), fire() and moveBullets() bodies have only STEP comments where the work goes: missing on every criterion. Write each note for THIS student's own code, for a 14-year-old reader: short sentences, plain words. In a not-met note, name the exact line or name in their code that causes the problem (quote at most a few words of it), say in plain words what it does now versus what the criterion needs, and give one concrete next thing to try, but do NOT write the corrected code. In a met note, say in one short phrase what in their code satisfied it. Do not use generic praise.

rubric.title: The ship stays on the canvas
rubric.description: After the ship moves, ship.x is held between 20 and 380 on BOTH sides: two ifs that set it back, an if/else if, constrain(ship.x, 20, 380), or max/min. Nearby limits (such as 18 and 382) are fine. Only one side held is partial. Limits that still let the ship leave the canvas (below 0 or above 400) are not met.

rubric.title: The cooldown counts down
rubric.description: Every frame fire() runs, cooldown goes down by 1 while it is above 0, and it does not run on below 0 (an if (cooldown > 0) guard, or max(0, cooldown - 1)). With no guard and a firing test of cooldown === 0, it is not met: cooldown would pass 0 into negatives, never equal 0 again, and the ship could fire only once. If the student's firing test asks cooldown <= 0 instead, an unguarded countdown still works and counts as met.

rubric.title: A shot is made only when Space is held and the cooldown is 0
rubric.description: The push of a new shot onto bullets sits inside a test that asks BOTH that Space is down (kb.pressing('space'), or kb.presses('space'), which fires once per tap) AND that cooldown has reached 0 (=== 0, <= 0, < 1, or !cooldown), joined with && or written as one if inside the other. A shot made on Space alone, or on the cooldown alone, is not met.

rubric.title: Firing sets the cooldown again
rubric.description: In the same block that pushes the shot, before or after the push, cooldown is set to 12 or any number above 0 (or a named constant), so the next shot has to wait. Setting it to 0, or setting it outside that block so it refills every frame, is not met.

rubric.title: Shots that leave the top are deleted and spliced out
rubric.description: Inside moveBullets()'s loop, an if that asks whether the shot's y has gone above the top (less than -20, or another value near the top such as less than 0) both deletes the shot's sprite (.delete() or .remove()) and splices it out of bullets at that index. Only one of the two is partial: a spliced shot that is not deleted stays on screen, and a deleted shot left in bullets keeps counting. A test with > (a y below the bottom) is the opposite and not met.
